digest_pinned_carry_chain.checked_in_code: yes: _digest_pinned_json_uncached sha256-compares each hop's receipt bytes to record.receipt_sha256; a missing/unreadable receipt, digest mismatch or repeated receipt ends the walk; later hops come only from the pinned receipt's own obligations[].carried_forward_from
digest_pinned_carry_chain.why: the pin has no independent anchor. resolve_carry_forward sets receipt_sha256 = sha256_file(path) for the receipt it selects (verdict ACCEPTED, family, artifact name, schema), so a substituted or edited receipt is self-pinned on a fresh run. Control f1 (modified receipt, stale pin) refuses; control f2 (same receipt, pin recomputed by the production rule) discharges. The b78b chain is evidence/closure-ssh-b78.json (sha256 c255b86a..., reproduced) -> evidence/closure-ssh-b76c.json (pinned inside the b78 receipt) -> head 0238c6e4ad; both anchors are computed from working-tree evidence, not compared to a committed manifest. The tool never reads court/freeze-b78/receipt-digests-b78.json
digest_pinned_carry_chain.additional: chain heads are only checked with git cat-file -e (existence), not ancestry of the candidate span_source_commit; _digest_pinned_json also accepts an absolute receipt path

ancestor_coordinate_is_definition_line.checked_in_code: yes: resolve_operation_at_line(root, file, item, hop.line, source_commit=head); span.def_line != hop.line is skipped; a coordinate inside a body resolves to the definition but fails the equality; an ambiguous coordinate refuses

ancestor_body_equals_boundary_recorded_h.checked_in_code: yes: hits are filtered to span_sha256 == boundary.span_sha256; all resolving hops must agree (len(set) > 1 -> None); the unchanged candidate check recorded != boundary_span.sha256 still runs after the migration binding

ancestor_body_equals_boundary_recorded_h.caveat: load_boundaries reads span_sha256 from the boundary receipt with no digest pin on that receipt, so the 'recorded' side of this equality is only as trustworthy as the evidence directory

uniqueness_exactly_one_boundary.notes: the map includes non-discharging and superseded boundaries (over-refusal only) and is keyed by boundary id (same-id duplicates collapse; no false discharge found from that)

different_operation_with_same_name.checked_in_code: partially: resolve_operation_span refuses an unqualified name with several definitions and selects by qualifier when one matches; migration_bindings filters only by scope_item (last component)
different_operation_with_same_name.sound: NO: nothing compares the ancestor hit's qualified identity with the boundary's resolved qualified identity or the candidate resolved identity, so a boundary can bind a row whose ancestor coordinate was a different qualified operation when the two bodies are byte-identical
different_operation_with_same_name.observed: control a DISCHARGED: boundary m2::copyctx, ancestor coordinate the definition line of m1::copyctx, identical bodies; the witness recorded ancestor line 2 and candidate line 11
different_operation_with_same_name.realized_rows_impact: none demonstrated: all 6 copyctx definitions in src/provider/digest.rs and both in src/provider/legacyprov.rs have distinct candidate hashes (recomputed), and the seven rows' operations are the qualified operations at the recorded coordinates. The gap is a property of the mechanism, not a changed verdict in these seven

re_admitting_a_prior_refusal.checked_in_code: the arm is reached only when resolve_operation_at_line fails with span-unparsable at the candidate coordinate; the content_accepts path then still applies disposition_discharges, conflict detection, the candidate recorded-hash check, and the uniqueness check. There is no persisted 'refused' state and no check of a prior closure's verdict
re_admitting_a_prior_refusal.sound: conditionally: it deliberately re-admits the coordinate-refusal class (the seven rows) and cannot re-admit a withdrawn/RETAINED disposition (control e), a current-hash mismatch (d), a tampered pin (f1), an ambiguous identity, or a row coordinate the chain does not name. It does not consult supersession for admission, so a boundary withdrawn only by a same-operation BLOCKED disposition in another receipt still discharges under the default ENFORCE_DISPOSITION_CONFLICTS=False; that gate is pre-existing, not introduced here

verdict.seven_rows: On the migration mechanism's evidence the seven must return to BLOCKED: the mechanism has a reproduced false bind (control a), no independent input anchor (f2) and an unchecked qualification assumption. They may remain DISCHARGED only if the closure explicitly cites the independent per-row content proof in evidence/b78-review-migrated-rows.json (which recomputed ancestor and candidate hashes and re-read the callers) and records that the migration binding itself is not the discharge evidence; the review's migration_binding_not_relied_on=true is exactly that separation. As currently produced, evidence/closure-ssh-b78b.json and evidence/closure-sshd-b78b.json present the 290/290 as tool output, so for closure purposes the seven are BLOCKED until the tool is repaired or the closure is re-issued with the per-row evidence binding
verdict.why_not_documentation: the missing qualified-identity comparison is a hidden obligation discovered by an adversarial control, not a documentation gap. Section 7 criterion 1 and the section 6 STOP condition (new hidden obligation) apply
verdict.what_the_seven_rows_do_establish: for each of the seven, the recorded coordinate was the definition line of the same qualified operation at ancestor head 0238c6e4ad; the normalised body there hashes to the boundary's recorded span; the candidate definition has the same hash; the candidate census attributes the operation to the resolved definition line; the caller/contract was re-read at b78 (evidence/b78-review-migrated-rows.json). That is a content proof. It is not a proof that the instrument's migration path is sound

required_additional_obligations: O1 qualified-operation agreement: require the ancestor hit's qualified_identity to equal the candidate resolved qualified_identity (and the boundary's qualified operation), or refuse the migration; scope_item alone is insufficient
O2 ancestry: require the hop head to be an ancestor of (or equal to) the candidate span_source_commit (git merge-base --is-ancestor), not merely to exist in the object database

O3 evidence-input integrity: bind the boundary receipts' digests (the source of span_sha256) and the carry-forward closure's digest to a committed manifest or freeze and check that manifest in the tool; do not compute the only pin from the file selected at run time
O4 fail closed when source_commit is unset: a migration bind must not be available when the candidate head is unknown, because the 'skip the candidate head' guard is then disabled

O5 per-hop refusal reasons: record receipt-missing / pin-mismatch / not-the-definition-line / body-hash-mismatch / census-absent / non-unique-owner on the obligation; today f1 and c both surface only span-unparsable
O6 uniqueness scope: decide and document whether non-discharging siblings may block an owner (currently they do), and key the map by (receipt, id) or boundary object rather than id alone
O7 path confinement: _digest_pinned_json should reject an absolute receipt path; a carry pin is evidence only if it names a repository-relative evidence file
residual_risks: the b78b closures were produced with tracked_tree_dirty=true at repository_head 6cdf9859 while joining obligations at span_source_commit bb7d5206; the operative identity is the source-content digest, not the commit

the carry-forward source for b78b is the same-artifact closure evidence/closure-ssh-b78.json (sha 3b282f43 for both runs). The discovery path would have skipped a same-sha closure; only an explicit --carry-forward-closure selects it, and that selection is process evidence, not a property the tool enforces

the default ENFORCE_DISPOSITION_CONFLICTS=False means a boundary withdrawn only by a conflicting BLOCKED disposition can still discharge; migration does not strengthen this and does not consult supersession on admission
the self-test for f31816b1 is NOT_RUN (no stored log after commit bd518a214); this review's controls are direct function-level evidence, not a self-test pass
the seven-row content proof is source-level: no build, Miri, ASan or runtime control ran at this candidate (section 6.1 floor not met; available 12 GiB)

the migration witness records only the chosen ancestor, not the rejected hops; a future edit to the ancestor or to the candidate body is still caught by the span hash, but the reasoning trail is thinner than the uniqueness check implies
what_this_does_not_establish: that any of the seven operations is or is not memory-safe at runtime; this review is instrument-level
that the seven rows' caller/contract analysis is correct beyond reading evidence/b78-review-migrated-rows.json
that SAFE_COMPATIBLE is established for ssh or sshd; the closures and the promotion assessment both record safe_compatible=false
that the element-7/ABI changes in the same tool diff are sound; they were classified for verdict impact only
that any other row reached by the migration path is correctly discharged; none was found beyond the seven, but the mechanism is refused here
